$comment: Human declarations about PUBLISHED contracts. This file is hand-authored; contracts/api-contract-registry.json
is generated OUTPUT and is never hand-edited. A declaration made here reaches the registry by running
Every entry states what the code actually does, verified by reading the handler named in `evidence`.
`at-least-once-unfenced` is a finding, not an endorsement: it records that the operation has no server-side
replay fence, so a consumer that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate. Recording it truthfully is
what lets the gate pass while leaving the defect visible; inventing a fence that does not exist would not.
Note that @Idempotent(command) is inert on unauthenticated routes -- idempotency.interceptor.ts falls through
to next.handle() unfenced when the request carries no orgId/userId -- so no @Public() route can be made
idempotent by adding that decorator alone.

`webhookEvents` declares subscribable outbound event names that no literal dispatch site spells out -- a dispatcher called with a variable, or an enum of subscribable triggers. Names emitted from a literal call site are discovered by the scanner and must NOT be repeated here.

idempotencyModes.safe: Read-only. Derived automatically from the HTTP method; never declared here.
idempotencyModes.idempotency-key: Fenced by @Idempotent(command) on command_fences (org, audience, Idempotency-Key). Derived from x-idempotent; never declared here.
idempotencyModes.provider-signature-and-event-id: Signature verified, then the provider's event id is stored under a unique constraint. A redelivery is a no-op.
idempotencyModes.provider-signature-idempotent-effect: Signature verified; no event id is stored, but the write converges (upsert or re-sync).
idempotencyModes.single-use-token: A conditional UPDATE ... WHERE <still-unused> RETURNING consumes the token exactly once; zero rows is an error.
idempotencyModes.single-use-token-racy: The same intent, expressed as a read-then-write. Sequential replays are refused, concurrent ones are not fenced.
idempotencyModes.natural-key-upsert: The write is an upsert on a natural key, so replays converge without a token being consumed.
idempotencyModes.advisory-dedup-unfenced: A SELECT-then-INSERT dedupe with no unique index behind it. Racy under concurrency.
idempotencyModes.replayable-write: An in-place write that a replay overwrites with the same values.
idempotencyModes.optimistic-concurrency: Lost-update protection via an expected-version field. Not replay protection.
idempotencyModes.captcha-single-use: The provider's single-use CAPTCHA token is the de facto fence.
idempotencyModes.no-persistence-rate-limited: No business write; a replay costs budget, not data.
idempotencyModes.at-least-once-unfenced: No server-side dedupe. A retry duplicates. Recorded so consumers and reviewers can see it.
idempotencyModes.provider-signature-only: Signature verified, and nothing behind it fences a replay — the event id is either not recorded, or the attempt to record it does not work. Like `at-least-once-unfenced`, a finding rather than a mode to copy: it is how a route reads when its dedupe was written but never fired.

GET /public/sign/forms/{slug}.sunsetEvidence: RETIRED WITH NO REPLACEMENT alongside its submit half — see POST /public/sign/forms/{slug}/submit for the dependency proof. This half was the anonymous reader of a published sign_public_forms row; migration 0660b dropped the table, so there is nothing left for it to read.

idempotency.replay: expectedUpdatedAt is compared to the stored updatedAt and a mismatch raises a conflict. This is lost-update protection, not replay protection, and the field is optional — an agent that omits it gets neither.

A pre-read outside the transaction refuses any offer whose status is not SENT or VIEWED (409), and the write moves it to a terminal status. The guard is a read-then-write, not a conditional UPDATE, so concurrent responses are not fenced.
Answers are deleted and re-inserted per question id inside one transaction, so replaying the same payload converges. Refused once the session leaves 'in_progress'.

Last-write-wins replacement of the whole scene on project_whiteboards; replaying the same payload converges on the same state. The share token is reusable and the write is unauthenticated when publicAccess='editor'.

When the caller supplies `key`, uniq_projects_org_key rejects the duplicate with 409. When `key` is omitted the key is randomly generated, so a retry silently creates a second project — callers that need retry safety must send an explicit key.
Bare insert into tickets with a sequential ticket number. A retry creates a second ticket. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
Bare insert into ticket_comments. A retry creates a duplicate comment. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
A SELECT on (candidate_id, job_posting_id) returns {alreadyApplied:true} instead of inserting, but no unique index backs it — concurrent retries can both insert.
The unsubscribe token is HMAC-signed and stateless — it is never marked consumed — but the write is onConflictDoUpdate on (org_id, contact_id, channel), so replays converge on the same consent row.

The RFC 8058 one-click form of the entry above: the token moves into the path so a mail client can post it with no body, and all three verbs share one `honour()` implementation. Same fence — onConflictDoUpdate on (org_id, contact_id, channel) — so the consent row converges on replay. The crm_contact_consent_events history row beside it is an unconditional insert, so a replay does append a second audit entry.
x-mailbox-signature verified against crm_mailbox_sync.push_secret. The handler re-runs a watermarked sync rather than writing, so a duplicate push converges instead of duplicating.

Bare insert into form_submissions (and a ticket when the form's actions create one) inside one transaction, rate limited per client IP. A retry after a timeout creates a second submission. No server-side replay fence.

Insert into csat_responses whose only unique index is (org_id, id), so nothing dedupes a resubmission and a retry records a second rating. `@UseRateLimit("csat:submit")` bounds the cost of that, not the duplication. The publicToken authenticates WHICH survey is being answered; it is not consumed and is not a replay fence.

Unauthenticated insert into csat_responses keyed only on a numeric survey id — no token, no dedupe, no handler rate limit. A retry creates a second response. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.

POST /csat/{surveyId}/responses.sunsetEvidence: REPLACED BY POST /csat/public/{publicToken}/responses, and removed as a security fix rather than a rename. The surveyId in this path is the table's serial primary key on a @Public() route, so any caller could count upwards and submit against another tenant's survey; migration 1089 records that csat_surveys was deliberately left off the 0384 public-read arm for exactly that reason. The replacement is keyed on the unguessable public_token the table already minted (uniqueIndex idx_csat_surveys_token), which is what let 1089 give csat_surveys the same public-token policy arm agent_tokens and api_keys carry. Same request body, same 201, same rate-limit tier; only the path segment changed. Retired in 2183bace9 (2026-09-11) together with that migration.

idempotency.replay: GitHub HMAC or GitLab token verified, then the delivery id is inserted into git_webhook_seen_deliveries with onConflictDoNothing on uniq_git_webhook_seen_deliveries_delivery. If the provider omits the delivery header the dedupe is skipped and the delivery is processed at-least-once.

Bare insert into leads with no conflict target and no natural key; ApiKeyGuard authenticates but does not deduplicate. A retried ingest creates a second lead. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
Stateless HMAC token, not single-use. The write is onConflictDoNothing on (org_id, email, channel) in email_suppressions, so replays converge.
UPDATE invitations SET status='ACCEPTED' WHERE id=? AND status='PENDING' AND accepted_at IS NULL RETURNING; zero rows raises 404. The token is matched by tokenHash and is consumed exactly once.
UPDATE invitations SET status='DECLINED' WHERE id=? AND status='PENDING' RETURNING; zero rows raises 404. Consumed exactly once.

Bare insert into platform_messages with a fresh random public code; rate limiter public:contact only. A retry creates a second message. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.

The pre-read requires status='PENDING', but the consuming UPDATE portal_invitations SET status='ACCEPTED' carries no status predicate and no affected-row check. Sequential replays are refused by the read; concurrent ones are not fenced.

Bare insert into change_requests; auth is the portal session token only. A retry creates a duplicate change request. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.

The candidate row is onConflictDoNothing on (org_id, email), but the candidate_applications insert is unconditional and mints a new tracking token. A retry creates a duplicate application. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
Turnstile token verified server-side and single-use provider-side; nothing is persisted, the effect is one outbound email. A replay with a fresh token re-sends it.

Bare insert into feedbucket_submissions with no conflict target; auth is the widget public key. A retry creates a second submission. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
No business write; rate limiters feedbucket:ai-assist and feedbucket:ai-assist-daily only. A replay spends model budget.

Bare insert into form_submissions; the collector token is reusable and never consumed. A retry creates a second submission. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.

Validated then inserted as a new submission row; no natural key and no token consumption. A retry creates a second submission. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
Bare insert into intake_items keyed only on the project id. A retry creates a second item. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
UPDATE interview_booking_links SET status='booked' WHERE id=? AND status='pending' RETURNING; zero rows raises 410 Gone. Consumed exactly once.
No business write; rate limiter ai:public-kb-ask only. A replay is safe for data but spends model budget.
No business write; rate limiter ai:public-kb-ask only. A replay is safe for data but spends model budget.
onConflictDoNothing on (org_id, article_id, visitor_id), counter bumped only when a row was inserted. visitor_id falls back to the client IP, so a replay from the same visitor is absorbed.
Bare mirrored-lead insert; the collector token is reusable. A retry creates a second lead. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.

Bare insert into nps_responses; the public token is reusable and never consumed. A retry creates a second response. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
A SELECT on external_referrers returns the existing referral token instead of inserting. Advisory only; no unique constraint is quoted.
A SELECT on (referrer_id, candidate_id) returns {alreadyReferred:true} instead of inserting. Advisory only; no unique index backs it.
Bare insert into feedback_posts. A retry creates a second post. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
insert(roadmap_votes) with onConflictDoNothing on the voter key; the vote counter is incremented only when a row was actually inserted, so a replay neither double-votes nor double-counts.

Each submission instantiates a fresh envelope from the template; the slug is a reusable public form address, capped only by maxSubmissions. A retry creates a second envelope. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.

POST /public/sign/forms/{slug}/submit.sunsetEvidence: RETIRED WITH NO REPLACEMENT, deliberately and with dependency proof. e371758b3 records the sweep: every frontend ref for this path on every branch returns only the generated openapi.json — the public form page app/(public)/forms/[token] calls /public/forms/:token, which is the BUILD module's forms feature and a different endpoint. The removal is a removal rather than a deprecation because the route was an unauthenticated WRITER: class-level @Public(), and it instantiated a template into a real envelope, flipped it to sent, minted a live signing token and handed that token back. It was reachable only in principle — a request needs a published sign_public_forms row and no UI ever created one, so every call 404'd — which is dormancy by absence of data, not by a guard. Migration 0660b then dropped sign_public_forms itself, taking the table's public-token read arm from 0384 with it.

idempotency.replay: Stores the adopted signature on the recipient row in place; a replay overwrites it.
Authenticates the recipient against the current OTP and updates the recipient row in place; replayable without creating additional state.

UPDATE sign_recipients SET status='completed', token_revoked_at=now() WHERE id=? AND status='authenticated' RETURNING; zero rows raises 400 'already completed'. The signing token is revoked by the same statement.
Records e-signature consent on the recipient row in place; a replay writes the same values.
UPDATE sign_recipients SET status='declined', token_revoked_at=now() WHERE id=? AND status=<observed> RETURNING; zero rows raises 400. The signing token is revoked by the same statement.
Field value upsert keyed on the recipient and field; a replay overwrites the same field rather than appending.
Re-issues a one-time code against the same recipient row; a replay supersedes the previous code rather than creating a second signature.

Bare insert into survey_answers, guarded only by the session's current question. A retry records a second answer. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.

Bare insert into survey_response_sessions returning a participant token. A retry creates a second participant. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.

Inside the transaction the session status must be 'in_progress' or the request is refused with 400 'already submitted'; the check is a read-then-write, not a conditional UPDATE. Answer writes are delete-then-insert per question and therefore replay-safe.
Bare insert into survey_response_sessions. A retry creates a second session. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
onConflictDoUpdate on platform_waitlist.email — a replay updates the same row rather than creating a second entry.

Mints a fresh inbound secret and creates a new support ticket on every call. A retry creates a second ticket. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
Resolves the ticket by session token and appends unconditionally. A retry appends a duplicate message. No server-side replay fence: a client that retries after a timeout must expect a duplicate.
UPDATE support_csat_requests SET responded_at=now() WHERE id=? AND org_id=? AND responded_at IS NULL RETURNING; zero rows raises 409. Consumed exactly once.

x-webhook-secret compared to support_channels.inbound_secret (401). Dedupe is a SELECT-then-INSERT on support_ticket_messages.source_message_id backed by idx_support_ticket_messages_source_message, which is NOT unique, so two concurrent redeliveries can both insert.

Svix signature (svix-id/svix-timestamp/svix-signature) verified before parsing. No provider event id is stored; the effect is an email_suppressions upsert with onConflictDoNothing on (email, channel), so a redelivery converges to the same state.

idempotency.key: the carrier's own event id, or a SHA-256 digest of the raw body when it sends none
idempotency.replay: The per-carrier shared secret selected by the orgId in the path signs the raw bytes; a bad signature is 401 and is recorded as a verification failure. Past that, the delivery is claimed by inserting into inv_carrier_webhook_deliveries with onConflictDoNothing on (org_id, carrier_id, event_key), which is the unique constraint uniq_inv_carrier_webhook_deliveries_event, so a redelivery returns 200 {ok:true,duplicate:true} and applies nothing. When the carrier supplies no event id the key is a digest of the body, so a byte-identical redelivery still dedupes but a re-sent event carrying a new timestamp does not — applyEvent's monotonic rule is the second guard there, and a callback arriving after DELIVERED changes nothing.

Provider signature verified before parsing (401 on failure), then the provider event id is inserted into payment_webhook_events with onConflictDoNothing on the unique index uq_payment_webhook_events_provider_env_event. A redelivery of the same provider event is a no-op.
Legacy URL alias for the payments webhook; same signature check and same uq_payment_webhook_events_provider_env_event fence. The event id is read from the body, not a header.

The platform's own STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET verifies the raw body before anything is parsed (401 on failure, 503 when Stripe is unconfigured so the delivery is retried), and an event type outside the translated set is acknowledged without being recorded. The dedupe behind that does NOT work today: recordEvent inserts into provider_webhook_events with onConflictDoNothing targeting (provider, provider_event_id), but migration 0605 replaced that unique index with (org_id, provider, provider_event_id) to close a cross-tenant DoS, so Postgres can infer no arbiter and the insert raises 42P10 on every money-moving delivery. So a redelivery is neither deduped nor processed — it errors. Reported by check:conflict-targets at src/modules/billing/core/stripe-webhook-ledger.ts:111; when the target is widened to include orgId this becomes provider-signature-and-event-id and this note must be rewritten.

idempotency.key: externalEventId + providerUpdatedAt, against the stored event
idempotency.replay: A sequential redelivery is refused twice over: handleScoped discards when the stored calendar_events.updatedAt is already >= the delivered providerUpdatedAt, and again when a PENDING or IN_FLIGHT row already exists in calendar_provider_sync_queue for that event. Neither guard fences CONCURRENT deliveries: the pending-queue SELECT and the queue INSERT run in two separate runInNewTenantTransaction calls and calendar_provider_sync_queue carries no unique constraint (only two non-unique indexes), so two deliveries racing past the same watermark each enqueue a sync row. The shared-secret header authenticates the caller; it is not a replay fence.
